artifacts.summary: 12-phase implementation plan for forward-chaining proof generation system. Phases: (1) extend instantiateAxiom to 42 schemata with Axiom witnesses, (2) ForwardConfig + ProofPool data structures, (3) instantiateAxiomWithProof returning DerivationTree witnesses, (4) modus ponens via O(n) implication index, (5) Nec/TempNec/TempDuality closures, (6) bounded fixpoint loop with ex_falso cap, (7) GenerationMode inductive dispatching in labelFormula, (8) ProofFirstExporter for JSONL output, (9) ProofFirstBenchmark computing 8 cross-corpus metrics, (10) CLI executable in lakefile.lean, (11) integration tests in BimodalTest/, (12) side-by-side comparison report. Total 20 hours, ~1295 LOC new + 180 LOC modified, organized into 6 dependency waves for parallel execution.

memory_candidates.content: Architectural pattern: forward-chaining proof generation in a dependently-typed proof assistant. Reuse the existing DerivationTree inductive (no new proof type); generalize the existing 'generate then drop proofs' generator (e.g., FormulaEnumerator.lean:1361) into 'generate and thread DerivationTree witnesses' by (1) extending instantiateAxiom to all 42 axiom constructors with Sigma-returning witnesses, (2) using shortest-height dedup via HashMap<Formula, Nat> for O(1) per insertion, (3) using a HashMap<Formula.lhs, Array<rhs, proof>> implication index for O(n) modus ponens closure instead of O(n^2), (4) capping ex_falso at 20% by mirroring the capExFalso logic, (5) frame class filtering at instantiation time (not at DerivationTree.axiom construction) to avoid runtime decide() calls. This pattern produces 100% valid labeled theorems (Lean type system IS the verifier) with configurable depth-based complexity control, expected ~37x improvement in valid-formula throughput vs. exhaustive enumeration.
